title: The EU AI Act Essentials
summary: You will be able to apply Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 across real policy and compliance scenarios: territorial and actor scope, Article 5 prohibited practices, Annex I and Annex III high-risk classification, provider and deployer obligations, Fundamental Rights Impact Assessments, General-Purpose AI and systemic risk rules, conformity assessment, governance and administrative fines.
prompt: The EU AI Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689) for AI policy and compliance professionals

modules.title: Scope, Actors and Phased Timeline
modules.objective: Determine when Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 applies across AI systems, value-chain actors, extraterritorial outputs, statutory exclusions, and phased application dates under Articles 2, 3, 4, 111 and 113.

modules.title: Prohibited AI Practices (Article 5)
modules.objective: Identify the eight prohibited AI practices under Article 5 and apply their narrow statutory exceptions, judicial authorization rules, and harm thresholds.
concepts: social scoring and criminal risk profiling
facial scraping emotion recognition and biometric categorisation

modules.title: High-Risk AI Classification (Article 6, Annex I and Annex III)
modules.objective: Classify high-risk AI systems under Annex I product safety legislation and Annex III standalone domains, including the Article 6(3) non-materiality filter and profiling override.

modules.title: Provider Obligations for High-Risk Systems (Articles 8 to 22)
modules.objective: Apply the lifecycle technical, data governance, documentation, logging, human oversight, robustness, and quality management obligations imposed on providers of high-risk AI systems.

modules.title: Deployers, Value-Chain Shifts and Fundamental Rights Impact Assessments
modules.objective: Distinguish deployer operational obligations under Article 26, Fundamental Rights Impact Assessments under Article 27, and when downstream actors become high-risk providers under Article 25.

modules.title: Transparency Rules and General-Purpose AI Models (Articles 50 to 56)
modules.objective: Apply Article 50 user-facing transparency duties and the Chapter V regime for general-purpose AI models, including systemic-risk designation at 10^25 FLOPs, open-source exemptions, and codes of practice.
concepts: article 50 interaction and synthetic media disclosure
gpai baseline provider duties and copyright policy
systemic risk threshold and article 55 obligations

modules.title: Conformity Assessment, Standards, Sandboxes and Incident Reporting
modules.objective: Navigate harmonized standards, internal versus third-party conformity assessment, CE marking, regulatory sandboxes, real-world testing safeguards, and serious-incident reporting timelines.
concepts: harmonized standards and article 43 conformity assessment
ce marking declaration of conformity and eu database
post-market monitoring and article 73 incident deadlines

modules.title: Governance, Enforcement, Penalties and Cross-Border Impact
modules.objective: Explain the enforcement architecture across the AI Office, EAIB, and national authorities, calculate administrative fine caps under Articles 99 to 101, and assess compliance impacts for Canadian organizations.
concepts: ai office eaib and scientific panel
national competent authorities and market surveillance
article 99 to 101 fine tiers and sme caps
canadian cross-border compliance and adequacy interplay
